facts.text: Mason earned its name from Stevens T. Mason, Michigan’s first governor, who helped shape the state’s early history.
In 1836, Stevens T. Mason cleared 20 acres of forest to establish Mason Center, the town’s original nucleus.
Mason’s first courthouse appeared in 1843, and by 1858 the town boasted sawmills, carriage factories, copper shops, a steam flourmill, and a buffalo robe manufacturer.
The historic Pink School, erected in 1859 at Columbia and College Roads, earned Michigan’s One‑Room Schoolhouse of the Year award.
The Mason Area Historical Museum at 200 E. houses the Virginia Schlichter Auditorium, where the society meets monthly from March through November.
Capital Area Transportation Authority buses run daily between Lansing and Mason, linking the county seat to the state capital.
